### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **55** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (9 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7c291ac65d11a4b3a25ca2acf3f501c9994d2acc` — the merge of head `cafbe826a8f6333b1f9db9f8ddda44a3a107528c` into base `bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7c291ac65d11a4b3a25ca2acf3f501c9994d2acc && git checkout 7c291ac65d11a4b3a25ca2acf3f501c9994d2acc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0 cafbe826a8f6333b1f9db9f8ddda44a3a107528c && git checkout -B drift-repro bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0 && git merge --no-ff cafbe826a8f6333b1f9db9f8ddda44a3a107528c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfc15d275ba3fed8406cd5836b826e617150fae0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

os-dev-report addendum (stage 3, post-stage-1 patch round) · cloud dev `session_01VUp6VuRm8SBjud6b5CwjSV` · 2026-10-11T02:21Z

Dispatched by epic PM `session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR` under claim amendment 6095710107; the task list is the landing condition of the seat's ACCEPT 6096484607. The PR body is left as written (one-write rule); this comment supersedes its "pending stage 1" section and its NOT MEASURED row.

**Head: `cafbe826a`** (pushed). Two commits on top of `ad45b7645b`:
- `12c7ea4b` merges `origin/main` at `bfc15d275ba3` (stage 1's squash). A plain merge: no conflict, and none of this PR's 7 files is a `merge=os-regen` path, so `os-regen-merge.sh` was not needed. Stage 2a's hunk in `security-plugin.ts` was not touched.
- `cafbe826` enables the pending case and corrects one stale setup comment (below).

**Size** against the new merge base `bfc15d275`: 1,289 changed lines (+1,274 / -15), 7 files, read from `dispatch-gates.mjs`. Under 3,000.

**The enabled case.** In `catalog-reference-report.test.ts`, `it.skip('PENDING STAGE 1: the removed declaration fails closed at the resolver, and re-adding it restores the grant', ...)` is now `it('the removed declaration fails closed at the resolver, and re-adding it restores the grant', ...)`. The PENDING comment is replaced by one saying why it holds. Result on the merged head: `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 13 passed (13)`, exit 0. It passed as written; no assertion changed.

**Premises re-verified on the merged head**

| Premise | Verdict |
|:--|:--|
| Item 2, "an unnamed grant confers nothing" | **true.** The resolver reads a grant's set by name and the set body from the catalog. The item-2 case passes and asserts that the resolver grants neither the set's name nor its bit. |
| Item 1, "a grant naming a set the catalog does not resolve confers nothing" | **true,** now also for a set whose row stays. The enabled case shows this. |
| Category 4, "assignments to a position with no definition distribute no permission set" | **true.** The resolver reads the position and its `permissionSets` from the catalog, so a `sys_position` row adds nothing. |
| Does any category read a table or an `active` flag that stage 1 stopped reading? | **No.** The report reads only names from `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set` and `sys_position`, and resolves each through `createSecurityCatalogReader`. It reads no `active` column and no junction row. `sys_position` is the read for categories 4 and 5. Those categories are about rows, not grants, so they hold. |
| `POSITION_OBJECT` and `metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName` exported from `position-write-through.ts` with the same meaning | **true.** `:108` and `:222`. Stage 1 changed only `saveDefinition` there: it now carries `permissionSets` through a row edit. |
| The report's catalog read matches the resolver's | **true.** The hook builds `createSecurityCatalogReader({ registry, metadata })` over the same engine registry and metadata service that stage 1 passes to `bindSecurityCatalogReader`. Both backfills beside it build theirs the same way. |
| Changeset sentences | **true;** no edit. |
| Test names and comments | **fixed, one.** `seedHolder`'s comment said the junction row is "the binding ... today". It now says the resolver reads only the definition, and that the junction row is left to show a leftover row keeps nothing alive. |
| PR body, "Landing order: after stage 1" and "The fail-closed half: pending stage 1" | **stale; superseded here.** Stage 1 has landed and the case is enabled. Under the one-write rule the dev does not edit the body. |
| Acceptance note: sharing rules expand position holders from `sys_user_position` | **still true** on `main`: `sharing-rule-service.ts:1447`, and `readPositionActive` at `:1606`. Stage 2b moves it. |

**Measured at `cafbe826a`.** Exit codes were captured before any pipe; heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: `Test Files 199 passed (199) · Tests 4139 passed | 45 skipped (4184)`, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`, which covers tsc, `tsconfig.scripts.json` and `check:test-typecheck`: exit 0 (test layer 0 errors).
- Dogfood `position-held-name-setup-create.dogfood.test.ts`, after building the `@objectstack/dogfood^...` closure: `Tests 4 passed (4)`, exit 0.
- Derived gates: `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 70 families against `bfc15d275`, and all 70 ran. `--ran` printed `70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)`. `check:startup-registry-verdict` and `check:durability-log-level` also ran, each exit 0.
  - In the first sweep, four commands refused on prerequisites and found nothing:
    - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3: its positive-control commit is outside the shallow clone.
    - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` exited 3: unbuilt packages.
    - `check:dts-closure` exited 1: `platform-objects` declarations were missing while a parallel build was still writing them.
  - After fetching that commit and building the workspace (turbo, 72 of 72 tasks), all four re-ran at exit 0, and those are the codes recorded.
- Not run locally: repo-wide `pnpm lint`, which belongs to CI.

**Open (to the PM, not built here):** a junction-only binding is invisible to this report. A position whose definition resolves, but whose sets are bound only through `sys_position_permission_set` rows, has distributed nothing since stage 1. Its names resolve, so the report reads clean. Converting those rows is C7b's job (#15211, `convertPositionBindingRows`), and release-cut condition (b) already depends on it. Per the dispatch, no category was added.
